summary: Grand Canyon Bar Ten Airstrip (GCT) is a remote private-use airstrip located on the Kaibab Plateau near the western edge of Grand Canyon National Park in northern Arizona. It primarily serves the adjacent Bar Ten Ranch, a working cattle ranch offering guest accommodations and guided trail rides into less-visited sections of the canyon. The dirt/gravel runway provides bush pilots with direct access to one of the most scenic yet isolated corners of the American Southwest.
faqs:
Q: Is Grand Canyon Bar Ten Airstrip open to the public?
A: The airstrip is primarily used by guests of the Bar Ten Ranch and is not a commercial facility. Prior permission or ranch booking is typically required before landing.

Q: What is the runway surface like at GCT?
A: The runway is an unpaved dirt and gravel strip suitable for small general aviation and bush aircraft. Pilots should check current condition reports before arrival.

Q: Are there fuel or maintenance services available?
A: No fuel, tie-downs, or maintenance services are available on-site. Pilots must plan to be self-sufficient for fuel and any aircraft needs.

Q: What is the elevation of the airstrip?
A: The airstrip sits at approximately 5,000 feet above sea level on the Kaibab Plateau, which can affect aircraft performance during summer heat.
transport_tips: There is no public road access to the airstrip itself; visitors typically arrive by air through Bar Ten Ranch arrangements or by ground vehicle to the ranch followed by ranch transport. The nearest town with services is Fredonia, roughly 40 miles to the north, while Kanab, Utah lies to the northeast. The nearest major commercial airport is Las Vegas Harry Reid International, about 170 miles southwest.
local_tip: Request a sunset horseback ride into the canyon during your stay; the Bar Ten is one of the only operations permitted to guide visitors on mules and horses down into the western canyon rim area, offering views unavailable from the more crowded South Rim.
